newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, dull period to last.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, dull period to last.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed in lacklustre trade on Friday to end the week mostly lower, and traders said dullness would continue to plague the market for some time.

Some traders ascribed the stagnation to the unstable political situation. Croatia this week saw the first popular protests in years and President Franjo Tudjman has been treated in a Washington hospital for alleged stomach cancer.
"People are afraid of possible political upheavals, of what is going to happen," a trader with Metroholding brokerage said.
But another trader with a large market share, citing the example of Zagrebacka Banka which traded well on Friday, said buyers were simply backing off as the festive season was approaching.
"People perhaps think there are smarter ways to spend your money than buying shares," he said.
All analysts agreed a period of stagnation, with no major price changes to shake the market, was likely to last.
Of seven active issues, two were up, three fell and two remained flat. Volume shrank to 3,386 units, while turnover slightly rose to 3.1 million kuna.
Total weekly stocks turnover fell to 30 million kuna from last week's 35.8 million. Most stock prices were down from last Friday.

Top decliner drugs firm Pliva plunged 850 kuna or almost seven percent, to close at 12,600 kuna on a meagre volume of 19 shares. Its GDRs fetched $49.935 in London. But traders said Pliva's low price was only temporary.
The other two decliners, hoteliers Istraturist and Jadranturist, lost 10 and 20 kuna, respectively. Selling 20 shares, Istraturist closed at 180 kuna, Jadranturist at 270 kuna, with 74 shares sold.
Zagrebacka Banka was one the few to hold its ground at 1,000 kuna throughout the week. It was Friday's most active issue with 2,712 shares sold. Its GDRs traded at $19.5 in London.

The only two gainers, cable maker Elka and hotelier Laguna, both inched up five kuna. Elka closed at 220 kuna, with 57 shares sold, while Laguna recovered to 1,150 kuna, with 484 shares changing hands.
Food processor Podravka was unchanged at 22o kuna, selling 484 units.
